Hi Sam — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Irene (privacy & legal ops) and Marissa (contracts) to surface the right reviewers and confirm signature flow. Quick answers up front:

- Subprocessors: we can accept a narrowed subprocessors clause if we add a standard notice-and-choice carve (Irene will propose exact language).
- SCCs: we sign the EU Commission standard processor SCCs; if you prefer the controller-processor set we can work with Legal to confirm the mapping, but processor SCCs are our usual path.
- SOC 2 evidence: we will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; security will also supply a short control matrix for encryption/key management.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Today — Redwood legal returns marked DPA with suggested substitute language (Irene).
2) Tomorrow — procurement sync (if needed) and Marissa sets up DocuSign flow for countersign once both sides agree.
3) By 24 Jul — target signature; if risk calls for exec sign-off we may need +48 hours.

Irene/Marissa — can you take point on the redline + SOC2 evidence location? I will confirm the DocuSign routing and the countersigner (Redwood execs) once we have agreed redlines.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — appreciated. A few clarifying points inline: 

> Proposed substitute language for subprocessors?

Procurement needs the sentence that gives FinBridge the right to require subprocessors to enter into equivalent obligations retained. If you can preserve that we can be flexible elsewhere.

> SCCs — we prefer the processor SCCs to be appended; controller SCCs will complicate our internal flow.

Noted. Regarding SOC2, procurement is OK to accept the report delivered under NDA; they asked if Redwood can provide a short letter confirming encryption settings (TLS1.2+, AES-256 at rest). A brief email from your security team should suffice.

Also please confirm the signers: FinBridge will sign via DocuSign (ProcureOps) and expects Redwood to countersign electronically. If Redwood needs executive signature we need to know who and whether a legal rep can sign.

Sam
